issue_title: Add POST /widgets/{id}/archive to archive a widget
issue_body:
Tenants want to hide widgets they no longer use without deleting them.

Add `POST /widgets/{id}/archive`. It sets `archived_at` on the widget and returns the updated widget. Archiving an already-archived widget returns 409. Archiving another tenant's widget returns 404. Archived widgets are excluded from `GET /widgets`.

Document the endpoint in api/openapi.yaml.

plan.summary: Add POST /widgets/{id}/archive, exclude archived widgets from the list endpoint, and document both.

approach.description: Add migration 0012 adding a nullable archived_at TIMESTAMPTZ column to widgets, with a matching down migration.
Add ArchiveWidget(ctx, tenantID, id) to internal/store/widgets.go returning ErrAlreadyArchived or ErrNotFound.
Add the POST /widgets/{id}/archive handler mapping ErrAlreadyArchived to 409 and ErrNotFound to 404.
Filter archived_at IS NULL in ListWidgetsByTenant.
Document the endpoint and its 200/404/409 responses in api/openapi.yaml.

verification.test_strategy: Handler tests for 200, 404 (other tenant) and 409 (already archived); a store test proving the list query excludes archived rows; the migration is exercised by the store test suite's migrate-up.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR. The change is additive; no data migration needs reversing.

acceptance_criteria.statement: POST /widgets/{id}/archive on an active widget returns 200 and the returned widget carries a non-null archived_at.
POST /widgets/{id}/archive on an already-archived widget returns HTTP 409.
POST /widgets/{id}/archive on a widget owned by another tenant returns HTTP 404.
After archiving widget W, GET /widgets no longer includes W.
POST /widgets/{id}/archive returns HTTP 429 after 10 requests per minute from one tenant.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Write endpoints should be rate limited to protect the database.

risks_and_assumptions: The migration is additive and nullable, so existing rows need no backfill.

catching_examples.note: ac-archive-rate-limit is inferred, but the issue never mentions throttling; its rationale is generic, not warranted by the issue.
The 429-after-10-requests criterion invents a rate limit no step implements and the issue never asked for.

non_catching_examples.note: No test covers archiving a widget id that does not exist at all (as opposed to another tenant's).
The OpenAPI change should also mark archived_at on the widget schema.
The down migration drops the column; any archived state is lost on rollback.
No test covers the rate limit resetting after the one-minute window.
Document the 429 response in api/openapi.yaml alongside 200/404/409.
A rate limited tenant could retry in a tight loop; add a Retry-After header.
